summary: The board glue is built like the hardware. Address decode, the PF/MO mixer and the daughterboard decode and banking go through per-GAL modules written as sum-of-products over numbered pin vectors. DTACK comes from a loadable wait-state counter, inputs from a 1-of-8 CIO decoder, and the outputs are strobed latches. Playfields are scanned pixel by pixel from the raster counter, and VRAM/CRAM model slot contention and posted writes, which MAME does not do. The VAD register block and the motion-object walker, though, follow MAME's atarivad/atarimo logic closely: the EOF copy loop that skips zero words, the update_parameter tag switch, the PF fine-scroll coupling, the visited[] link walk, and the ypos/xpos wrap formulas against a 336x240 bitmap. So the lean is moderately toward hardware.

findings.signal: GAL equations as sum-of-products with pin ports
findings.note: Each PAL is its own module with a 19-pin input vector and outputs 12-19. Outputs are inverted SOP terms, some registered on a clock enable, and each output has a separate drive (OE) vector, as in a fuse map.

findings.signal: Main decode via GAL pin adapter
findings.note: Chip selects (ROM, E0/E1, IOEN, wait selects) come from wiring A15-A21, /AS, EDT and VDTACK onto GAL pins, not from range compares like MAME's address map.

findings.signal: Mixer built from two GALs, not MAME's priority code
findings.note: The colour-RAM index is assembled from the registered outputs of the 3F/5F GAL models, with inverted pin polarities. MAME computes a simplified cs0/cs1 test in C and keeps a separate priority bitmap.

A 4-bit counter loads parallel data built from {VPA, handshake wait, 1, base wait} while count[2] is low, then counts up to terminal count to release DTACK. This is the board's carry/load counter structure; MAME has no wait states.

findings.signal: Discrete-style I/O: 138 decoder and strobed latches
findings.note: CIO selects are a 1-of-8 decode of MA6:4. The coin/sound-reset latch, volume (DVC) latch and 9-bit control latch capture the data bus on decoded strobe edges. MAME splits the same register by byte lane in audio_control_w and audio_volume_w.

findings.signal: Scan-time playfield pipeline from raster counters
findings.note: The tile column and row are latched every 8 pixels from px+xscroll. Code and attribute words are pipelined through a shift register and the plane bits are selected per pixel on ce_7m. There are no tile_info callbacks and no per-frame tilemap draw.

findings.signal: Bus contention and DMA cycle stealing
findings.note: VRAM uses fixed per-phase slots for PF code/attr, MO, CPU and DMA. CRAM has CPU/scan slots, posted writes gated by OVRDTACK/OCRDTACK, and O_DCDMA double-time cycles. All of this is VAD bus behaviour that MAME does not model.

findings.signal: EOF register update mirrors eof_update loop
findings.note: During vblank it walks indices 0..0x1B (EOF_LAST='h1B) and writes each word into the registers only when it is non-zero (EOF_SKIP_ZERO). This is the same loop and the same skip-zero test as MAME's `for (i=0;i<0x1c;i++) if (m_eof_data[i]!=0) internal_control_write`.

findings.signal: update_parameter tag switch and xscroll coupling
findings.note: Writes to 0x10-0x1B dispatch on data[3:0] (9/A/B/D/E/F) with value=data[15:7]. The other playfield's scroll adds pf1_xscroll[2:0], the same expression as MAME's `raw + (other_raw & 7)`.

findings.signal: MO list walk with visited[] bitmap
findings.note: A 256-bit visited array is cleared each line and checked per link to stop the walk. It is copied from MAME's `uint8_t visited[MAX_PER_BANK]` loop guard, not a hardware mechanism.

findings.signal: MO position math copied from render_object
findings.note: ypos = -y - yscroll - (height<<3), then if ypos >= BITMAP_H(240) subtract 512. xpos = x + xoff - xscroll, wrapped against BITMAP_W(336). These are MAME's steps against bitmap.height()/width(), the screen size, rather than a hardware counter compare.

findings.signal: VAD register map and beam readback
findings.note: Register indices, OPT bit fields (OPIUM, OAS_EN, OCRDTACK...) and the vpos readback clamped to 255 with vblank in bit 14 match MAME. A correct core must share these.
